market_context: Monday's Nvidia-led rebound is being faded: SPY was $713.76 pre-market, S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures were approximately 1.1% and 2.0% lower at 08:51 ET, and Nvidia was down about 5% after its 31% surge (finance.yahoo.com, raspberrytrades.com). The backdrop remains fragile, with VIX near 30, SPY still 7.6% below its high, and the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.89%; I expect profit-taking to produce a lower close led by technology, without fully retracing Monday's rally.

predictions.reasoning: Yahoo showed SPY at $713.76 pre-market, down 1.21%, while S&P futures were about 1.1% lower at 08:51 ET following Monday's 4.71% surge ([finance.yahoo.com, raspberrytrades.com). With volatility elevated and the broader trend still negative, I expect the opening discount largely to persist near Monday's $713.53 intraday low.

QQQ traded at $639.91 at 8:00 ET, down 1.71%, and Nasdaq-100 futures subsequently indicated roughly a 2% decline as chip stocks led the pullback (stocktitan.net, finance.yahoo.com). The premarket decline had surrendered only about a quarter of Monday's 7% gain, so my target allows for modest additional selling without assuming a complete reversal.

NVDA traded at $157.30, down 4.70%, at 8:01 ET after Monday's 31.48% jump; Micron was down 6.17% and HPE 11.88%, confirming broad AI and semiconductor profit-taking (stocktitan.net). Yahoo also reported Nvidia down approximately 5% alongside a 2% decline in Nasdaq futures, making a finish below Monday's $165.05 close more likely than a full intraday recovery (finance.yahoo.com).

Russell 2000 futures were down approximately 0.7% at 08:51 ET, substantially less than Nasdaq futures, while the 10-year yield at 4.89% remains a headwind for smaller companies (raspberrytrades.com). I therefore expect a modest pullback after IWM's 3.56% Monday gain rather than a technology-style retracement.
